page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading, the instance provides 32.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Architecture support includes the x86_64 instruction set alongside hardware capabilities such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA_NI cryptographic acceleration. Hyper-V hypervisor manages compute allocation, and no GPU accelerators are included.

Integrated local storage is delivered through a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, providing direct scratch space alongside support for premium remote storage disks. In benchmark evaluations, the E4ads_v6 demonstrates strong single-core stress-ng performance and solid text processing capabilities. However, multi-core throughput and memory-intensive metrics show trade-offs: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and redis SET operations place in lower benchmark tiers, while static web serving achieves an average throughput of 6.59 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation coupled with bundled high-speed local NVMe storage, making it suitable for memory-heavy tasks without provisioning larger core counts. The instance is suited for caching layers, in-memory databases requiring moderate compute concurrency, enterprise application runtimes, and local scratch-space workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD for fast transient storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread performance and text processing, while multi-core workloads, memory bandwidth, and database operations exhibit more modest throughput consistent with its 4-vCPU footprint. The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides resource efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise services, middleware, in-memory caches, and web application deployments needing high RAM without surplus compute cores.
